home.noAdminBody: Some system folders stay hidden, and the system cleaner is not available. For the folders in ~/Library, give Lustro Full Disk Access.

admin.unixHint: To get root rights, close Lustro and start it as root: sudo /Applications/Lustro.app/Contents/MacOS/lustro. For most folders, Full Disk Access is enough.

settings.protectedHint: The root folder, the system folders (/System, /usr, /Library, /Applications and others), home folders and their standard folders, ~/Library, SSH keys and the keychains. Lustro never deletes them.
settings.allowAppFoldersHint: Only as root. You can then delete apps in /Applications, with a warning each time. To remove an app with its data, use Apps > Uninstall.
settings.startWithWindowsHint: Starts in the menu bar, without root rights.

scan.deniedNote_one: macOS did not let Lustro read 1 folder. Give Lustro Full Disk Access in System Settings > Privacy & Security to include it.
scan.deniedNote_other: macOS did not let Lustro read {{count}} folders. Give Lustro Full Disk Access in System Settings > Privacy & Security to include them.

explore.appFolder: App in /Applications. You can delete it, but you must confirm a warning.
explore.appFolderLocked: App in /Applications. To remove it with its data, use Apps > Uninstall.
explore.denied: macOS did not let Lustro read this folder. Give Lustro Full Disk Access in System Settings > Privacy & Security.

del.appWarn_one: This item is inside /Applications. If you delete a part of an app, the app can stop working. To remove an app with its data, use Apps > Uninstall instead.
del.appWarn_other: {{count}} items are inside /Applications. If you delete parts of apps, the apps can stop working. To remove an app with its data, use Apps > Uninstall instead.

history.gone: No longer in the Trash, or renamed there

apps.uninstallDesktop: Moves the app and its data in ~/Library to the Trash.
apps.uninstallStore: Moves the app and its data in ~/Library to the Trash.
apps.note: Uninstall moves the app and its data in ~/Library to the Trash. You can restore them from the Trash.

live.off: Live updates are not available on macOS yet
